title: Water system FAT and SAT to EU GMP Annex 15 | Aquemi
meta: Wet FAT on every skid to a protocol you approve, then SAT on your feed water. Written to EU GMP Annex 15, 3.6 so IQ and OQ can leverage results.
eyebrow: FAT · SAT · EU GMP ANNEX 15 · GAMP 5
headline: Watch your water system run wet, against a protocol you approved, before it ships
lead: Every skid runs a wet factory acceptance test (FAT) to a protocol your quality unit approves, so installation and operational qualification (IQ/OQ) can leverage it (Annex 15, 3.6). Site acceptance testing (SAT) proves the rest.

secondary_cta.label: Arrange a test bay visit or audit

blocks.h: Found at FAT, a fault costs a day
body: Most start-up faults show only with water running: a valve opening in the wrong step, an interlock on the wrong input, a divert that never fires. Here the fix is a cable, a line of code or a fitting, made that afternoon. On your site it waits for a permit, a contractor and a production gap.

So every skid runs wet: pumps against real pressure, heated to sanitization temperature, conductivity and total organic carbon (TOC) measured at the outlet. Run to an approved protocol with calibrated instruments and raw data, it is supplier evidence you can leverage (GAMP 5, ASTM E2500). Run from a checklist, it gets repeated.

blocks.h: What a FAT cannot prove, however well run
blocks.body: Outlet quality at FAT is on our test water, not yours. Your feed water, utilities, network and field-built loop exist only on site, and microbial control is proven only by sampling through performance qualification (PQ).

blocks.h: Questions validation and quality teams ask

items.q: Will our quality unit accept FAT results in place of IQ/OQ tests?
items.a: That is its decision, and Annex 15 sets the test: appropriate, justified and unaffected by transport and installation. We mark candidate test cases in the commissioning and qualification plan at detailed design, your quality unit approves the protocol first, and the report carries calibrated instruments, raw data and signatures. Water quality on your feed and site utilities are never leveraged.

items.q: Can we use our own protocol template?
items.a: Yes. We write into your template and numbering, or deliver ours for you to adopt. Either way each test case carries a URS or functional specification reference, so it lands in your traceability matrix.

items.q: What if a test fails while you are watching?
items.a: It is recorded as found, as a deviation. We do not edit the acceptance criterion or quietly rerun the test; Annex 15, 2.7 treats a significant protocol change as a deviation too. We investigate, fix, and retest that case and any case the fix could affect, with you witnessing the retest.

items.q: Is the software we see at FAT the software that ships?
items.a: Yes. The programmable logic controller (PLC) and operator interface software is under version control, and its version and checksum are recorded in the protocol. Any change after FAT goes through change control with a stated regression test, and is shown again at SAT.

items.q: Do you FAT the distribution loop?
items.a: The loop pump and heat exchanger skid, the tank and the controls, yes. Loop piping is built on your site, so its slopes, branch lengths, welds and hydraulics are proven at SAT and IQ. See storage and distribution loops.

items.q: Can you test for endotoxin at FAT on a Water for Injection (WFI) system?
items.a: [endotoxin at FAT: offered, and which laboratory]. Like conductivity and TOC, it is a result on our feed water, so it supports, but does not replace, sampling on your site.
